headline: Chips Crater While Homebuilders and Software Surge in a Friday Full of Contrasts
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a sharply bifurcated note, with a pronounced rotation out of semiconductor names and into homebuilders and software stocks defining the day's dominant narrative. Of the 501 names in our universe, 299 finished higher against 200 decliners, a breadth reading that flatters the headline but obscures meaningful damage beneath the surface. Homebuilders led all sectors with a gain of 2.84%, followed by Software at 2.05%, while Semiconductors shed 5.2% — the week's most punishing sectoral move.

The geopolitical backdrop provided the session's most urgent context. U.S. military action against Iran, warnings to China and Russia against intervention, and predictions that Strait of Hormuz traffic may not normalize for a year or more sent physical oil prices surging toward the $110 mark in spot markets. Energy services stood as an unlikely beneficiary: Schlumberger rocketed 10.79% to top the gainer board, a reminder that supply-disruption anxiety can quickly reprice oilfield-services names that had been left for dead.

The standout decliner was MaxLinear, off 22.13%, dragging peers Sandisk and Power Integrations down 11.0% and 10.51% respectively. The session's closing observation is a simple one: when geopolitics tightens energy supply chains and simultaneously rattles AI-capex confidence, capital rotates fast — and Friday showed just how fast.

briefs.headline: Schlumberger's 10% Surge Stands Out in an Otherwise Bruised Energy Patch
briefs.body: Schlumberger surged 10.79% on Friday, making it the session's single biggest percentage gainer across the entire universe. The move came as escalating Middle East conflict drove fresh anxiety over upstream supply, lifting sentiment sharply for oilfield-services providers even as the broader Energy sector finished down 0.37% on the day.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Absorbs Its Worst Session in Weeks
briefs.body: The Semiconductors group shed 5.2% on Friday, the steepest sectoral decline of the session by a wide margin. MaxLinear's 22.13% collapse and double-digit drops at Sandisk and Power Integrations drove the carnage, with Coherent — an optical-networking supplier closely tied to data-center buildout — also falling more than 10%.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Disruption Could Stretch Well Into 2027, Markets Signal
briefs.body: Prediction markets now assign significant probability to Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic remaining constrained for twelve months or longer, according to aggregated forecasting data. The assessment compounds existing Red Sea disruptions and adds a new dimension of freight-cost risk for energy importers and manufacturers reliant on Persian Gulf supply lanes.

briefs.headline: Packaging Corp Jumps More Than 8% on Earnings Momentum
briefs.body: Packaging Corp posted the session's second-largest gain at 8.27%, reflecting investor enthusiasm for the company's latest results. The move underscored a quiet but persistent bid for industrial-packaging names, which have benefited from reshoring-linked demand and relatively stable input costs compared with more volatile materials subsectors.

briefs.headline: Hims & Hers Tumbles Nearly 15% as Telehealth Sentiment Sours
briefs.body: Hims & Hers Health fell 14.18% Friday, one of the session's sharpest single-stock declines outside the semiconductor complex. The sell-off extended a difficult stretch for consumer-facing telehealth platforms, which have faced mounting questions about competitive pressure and regulatory scrutiny in their core prescription categories.

briefs.headline: Asia LNG Prices Hit Four-Month High as Mideast Shipping Risk Widens
briefs.body: Asian liquefied natural gas spot prices climbed to their highest level in four months Friday, driven by market concern that escalating Middle East hostilities could further restrict tanker routes. At least one tanker operator redirected an Asia-bound voyage through the Suez Canal amid renewed Houthi warnings, illustrating the real-time rerouting calculus now facing energy shippers.
